hook: SCP-2664 is a Cold War weapon story told mostly through two voices: a defector explaining what his team built, and a task force reporting from inside the place where it was built. The file carries a breadcrumb into a larger series, The Coldest War, but reads on its own. Be warned that it describes children being drugged and electrocuted to death, and soldiers dying in grisly ways.
whyItMatters:
The premise flips the usual Soviet superweapon: officially a tool to make the world obey Moscow, secretly engineered by war-weary scientists to make people unable to fight. That gap between the order and the intent is what the whole file runs on.

It is also a strong example of an exploration log carried by a single relay. Because radios die at the door, everything the team sees reaches Command through one agent's borrowed voice, and the reader has only that thin, unreliable channel.
thingsToNotice:
Iceman's account is the key to the expedition: the triplets were dosed with LSD, forced to watch propaganda and electrocuted to death so their minds would separate from their bodies, and the Russian phrases that later come out of L9-7 are the soothing words and voltage orders from that very session. The last thing the weapon learned before death was that its makers planned a conjunction, and that is exactly what it does to the squad.

The log piles up quiet wrongness before the reveal: the endless helix, Four falling past again from the other side, a lab holding the corpses of all eight team members in lab coats, and the relay voice switching from One to Two to Three without anyone noticing at first. The facility, the space and the absorbed squad all turn out to be inside the entity's mind, which wants the whole world to join it. Decades later the growth spikes and kills everyone within 200 km, and only a Global Occult Coalition payload called Gaius Prime ends it, leaving the Foundation investigating that weapon instead.
